1_Learning_Objective.Title: 🎯 The "Why Are We Learning This?" (Learning Objective)
1_Learning_Objective.Content: Through a beautiful story, this chapter teaches your child the seven colors of the rainbow, encourages imagination, and links colors to natural objects (like flowers and leaves).

2_The_Hook.Title: 🪝 The Hook (How to start the conversation)
2_The_Hook.Content: Hold a glass of water near a sunny window to make a prism reflection, or just ask: **'Have you ever seen a magical, colorful bridge in the sky after it rains?'** Let them describe it. Say, **'Today we are reading about Anandi, a girl who loved rainbows so much, she decided to paint her garden with them!'**

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'A rainbow has 7 beautiful colors! Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red. They always come in a team.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Bring out a box of crayons. Have your child find those 7 specific colors and line them up side-by-side like a rainbow.

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'In the story, Anandi dreamed of a rainbow. When she woke up, she wanted to paint the flowers in her garden using the rainbow colors. She painted red roses, yellow sunflowers, and green leaves!'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Ask them: 'If you had Anandi's magic paintbrush, what in our house would you paint yellow? What would you paint blue?'

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Anandi painted with all the colors, except for Yellow. She left the yellow for the Sun, so it could shine brightly over her garden!'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Look up at the sky together (safely, not directly at the sun) and talk about how the sun is a giant yellow star that helps all the colorful flowers grow.

4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Title: 🚧 Common Stumbling Blocks (What to watch out for)
4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Content:
The colors **Indigo** and **Violet** are hard for 1st graders to understand as they just look like 'dark blue' and 'purple'. 
*   **How to clarify:** Tell them Violet is like the color of Brinjal (eggplant). Indigo is the deep color of blue jeans. Keep it simple and focus on 'Purple' and 'Dark Blue' if they struggle.

Questions.Question: What colorful thing did Anandi see in her dream?
What color did Anandi leave for the Sun?
Can you name three colors that live inside the rainbow?
Questions.Expected_Answer: (Any three: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet)

Activities.Name: 1. The Fruit Rainbow Plate
Activities.Description: Snack time! Make a mini edible rainbow. Use a strawberry (Red), a slice of orange (Orange), a banana (Yellow), and some grapes (Green). Eat the rainbow!

Activities.Name: 2. Rainbow Color Hunt
Activities.Description: Give them a basket. Tell them they have 3 minutes to run around the house and put one item of EACH rainbow color in the basket (e.g., a red block, an orange toy, a green leaf).

Activities.Name: 3. Water and Mirror Rainbow
Activities.Description: Put a mirror inside a glass of water at an angle. Shine a flashlight onto the mirror in a dark room to project a real mini rainbow onto the wall!

Activities.Name: 4. Cotton Ball Clouds
Activities.Description: Draw a rainbow outline on paper. Have your child color it in, and then glue fluffy white cotton balls at the ends of the rainbow to make clouds.
